decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The principle of the proposal development of a new dwellinghouse on garden land would not be acceptable, as national, regional and local planning policies make a presumption against such development due to the harm to the local spatial character that would occur, as in this case. The proposal involving the development of a new dwellinghouse on garden land fails to accord with policy LP7 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), the London Mayor's Housing SPG (2016) and the Wandsworth Housing SPD (2016).

Reason : 2 - The proposed dwelling, by reason of design, scale and location  would appear as a prominent, unsympathetic and incongruous form of development that would result in harm to the character and appearance of the existing property, streetscene and Totterdown Fields Conservation Area. Any such benefits amounting from the development would not outweigh the harm identified. The proposal therefore fails to comply with the NPPF (2024), policies LP1, LP3 and LP7 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023) and the guidance within the Housing SPD (2016) and Totterdown Fields CA Appraisal & Management Strategy.

Reason : 3 - The proposed development, by reason of the height and depth along the boundaries of nos. 99 and 97 Derinton Road would be an unneighbourly form of development that creates a pronounced sense of enclosure and appears overbearing to occupiers of neighbouring properties, resulting in harm to their residential amenity. As such, the development fails to comply with  policy LP2 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023) and the Housing SPD (2016).

Reason : 4 - Due to the discrepancies in the scales and dimensions shown on the proposed drawings, the proposed application fails to demonstrate that the dwellinghouse would meet minimal standards for gross internal area, bedroom size, exterior amenity space and ceiling heights, and therefore fails to demonstrate that the development would afford future occupiers with an acceptable standard of accommodation. As such, the development fails the requirements of policy D6 of the London Plan (2021), policies LP27 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), and the Technical Housing Standards - Nationally Described Space Standard (2015).

Reason : 5 - In dealing with this application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to make available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies in the Local Plan as well as offering a full pre application advice service. However, we have been unable to seek solutions to problems as the principle of the proposal is clearly contrary to our statutory policies and negotiation could not overcome the reasons for refusal.

Reason : 6 - INFORMATIVE: BNG APPLIES

In the absence of a Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment or Exemption Statement, the application fails to demonstrate that the application would be exempt from Biodiversity Net Gain. The applicant is advised that the effect of paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 is that planning permission granted for the development of land in England is deemed to have been granted subject to the condition ("the biodiversity gain condition") that development may not begin unless: a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the local planning authority, and; b) the local planning authority has approved the plan. There are statutory exemptions and transitional arrangements which mean that the biodiversity gain condition does not always apply. Based on the information available this proposal is considered to be one which will require the approval of a Biodiversity Gain Plan before development is begun because none of the statutory exemptions or transitional arrangements are considered to apply.
description: Erection of a single-storey dwelling with associated works, including new boundary treatments, landscaping and removal of tree.
